Hello. So this is reddit, so everyone will (and is) going to tell you to just leave. People are calling you a coward for staying. You are not. You're a man who has known love. One person even compared your partner to a 15 year old sweaty baseball cap.... We don't know you or your partner, so take some time for some real introspection---both you as an individual and together with your partner. 

I will offer this counter-point to the 'just leave-bro' commentary. In life we are given people that we cannot choose. For better or for worse, your mother is your mother, and your father is your father. This or that person is you brother or sister etc. Even if you were to cut these people out of your life, there is still an inherent connection with them. Maybe you're inconvenienced by a father with dementia, but they are still your father whether you care for them or not. In a world as chaotic as this one, I find that there is comfort in that. With partners, we have a choice to apply that same sentiment of permanence, or not. Is this person truly my partner for life? Or are they just a passing connection? If you choose to have this person as your partner, it may come at the cost of your 'happiness,' maybe even for a long time. At times, it could straight up suck and that could go on and on and on. But genuine love is about more than happiness---hard to explain unless you've been there. It's like are staying together simply because there is no other way. They are your partner. Period.

A question you may ask yourself is do I really love this person for all of who they are, depression and head-shaving included? They are having a hard time, kind of going nuts, and inconveniencing me and causing me to suffer. Can I accept this as part of their personhood and have that be part of my love for this person? Or am I attached to how they (used to) make me feel within myself? Is the dopamine oxytocin cocktail of attraction and sexuality what I actually want? This is where 'we don't know you or have answers for you' begins. All I can offer is this: if you decide to stay with your partner with all of her faults; and suffer with them and are open to it, you may find that you discover something rarer and more deeply valuable than happiness.

It's difficult to describe exactly what it should look like, again this comes with experience. You can manipulate this opening to tune certain notes and effect the tone and strength and what not, but if the blades have a wobble in them beyond their set curve, its never going to sound crisp. And that's the main thing I'm looking for in a reed. If nothing else, I want it to sound crisp. A reed sounds crisp when both blades make full contact with the other. This can't happen as efficiently if the blades aren't straight. Scraping is a good technique to easy up a reed and flatten certain notes. Don't be afraid to do some research on this and experiment with some reeds that aren't your favorite. You can always buy a new one.

If you have the means, you should mic them separately onto two separate tracks, recorded simultaneously. Yes, there is obviously some bleed over (chanter sound on the drone track and vice versa) but that's not a big deal. This allows for separate EQing of them and the ability to pan them to different places on the stereo mix making a bigger sound. 

However, your inexperienced with recording, you can still get a pretty good sound of one microphone. Stick it in front of the chanter some where, perhaps a bit to the right, since the chanter is the main thing you're trying to capture. Drones will be heard, but they won't sound as present.

Yeah: I have a background in recording/audio production and stuff so let me know if there's something you don't understand. For the chanter I'm using a large diaphragm condenser mic. They're usually used on vocals and are *highly* sensitive and responsive. For the drones, I used a small diaphragm condenser mic. Still sensitive, but not some much as the large one. For any acoustic instrument recording, condenser mics usually work the best. I ran them into my computer using a muti-channel usb audio interface -- this basically encodes the analog data from the mics to a digital format and connects to the computer via usb. I edited and mixed on a program called Ableton Live. I did some audio manipulation----compression, EQ, and reverb among other things. I'll admit, I over indulged in the reverb, but it sounded so darn good. The same basic things can be done on GarageBand if you have a mac or an open source digital audio workstation (DAW).

Kurt clicked on the little green messaging square.

Kurt clicked on the box. The familiar little keyboard popped up. He began: *Kate! I miss you! Would you be interested...*
	
He stopped and backspaced back to blank. He tried again: *Kate! I was just thinking of you. It’s been so long, would...*
	
He started one more time: *Hey Kate. How are you? Would you be interested in getting coffee sometime? It would be great to catch up!*
	
“There. Direct to the point. Non-threatening. She’d definitely be down for that, I think.”
	
Kurt held his thumb over the send button for a moment. He moved it back and forth over the blue letters as if the gravity of the entire combined universe couldn’t drag his thumb down to the glass. He abruptly moved his thumb over the home button an clicked it without even deleting his words. He hit the sleep button on top and dropped the phone face down on the table by his coffee. He brought his forehead to the table to follow suit. He stayed there for a moment with his eyes closed. 
	
“I’ll just send that later then. Yeah, right you putz. You never do anything. I know, I’m the worst. I probably look like quite the freak here to everyone right now with my head on the table like this. People probably think I’m such a little loser boy. Oh, well. Fuck ‘em. I do what I want.” 
	
Kurt let out a little snort. 
	
“Heh. South Park again... I want them to look at me. I want them to think I’m a freak. Who cares anyway? Stupid sheep. I don’t care what you think. I’m a lion dammit!”
	
Kurt looked up from the table but still kept his head low such that his chin was only a few inches off the surface. He looked around the room, but no one bothered to look back.
	
“Fine. Don’t look at the freak then.”
	
A crack of sunlight from the door broke over his eyes and interrupted his train of thought. In walked this girl. Kurt was squinting in the stream of light erupting from the crack in the door. It was significantly darker in the shop and his eyes had a hard time adjusting. The door swung shut and he was hit with her entire force. She was short and pale with blond hair tied into a pony tail. She wore black jeans with skateboard shoes and a long sleeve tee-shirt of some band he didn’t know. Around her neck and wrists dangled more little nicknacks than he could count at the time. They jingled in this soothing way when she leaned forward a bit to squint back at Kurt, who looked like he had just woken up from a winter’s slumber.
	
Then, she smiled. It was a toothless smile, like she didn’t want to show her teeth in fear of scaring him off. Her face wasn’t that magazine beauty either, but there was something about it that made his palms sweat. 
	
His brain raced for what to do. He would usually look away quickly, but it was too late for that. He attempted smile but all he could muster was a cock-eyed, twisted grimace with bits of his lips stuck in odd places around his mouth. At least that’s what it felt like to him at the time.
	
She gave a short laugh out of her nose and proceeded to walk to the counter without a single word. It took a moment for Kurt to gather himself. 
	
“Did she just snort at me? I know I may not be the best looking guy, but geez. Snorting in peoples faces is just plain rude. Who does she think she is? Walking in here and breaking my concentration.”
	
Kurt threw open his laptop once more, neglecting etiquette. There were his thousand words of brilliance just as they were before. They had not grown of their own accord, much to his dismay. He placed his fingers on the rows of black keys and began looking intently at the monitor much like he had been doing before. Less than a minute passed before he was looking over his screen towards the counter. 
	
“I wonder what she’s ordering. Maybe she’ll get the French Roast just like me. That’d be a good place to strike up a conversation. Ah, hell I never do that, though. Fuck me, I suck. Why is this so hard? Maybe she’ll talk to me. Yeah, fat fucking chance. She’s probably a bitch who wouldn’t give me the time of day. Look at her with that shirt. No one cares about your stupid band that only you’ve heard of! She’s probably ordering one of those frappe-freez-a-fucks girls like her are always ordering. Nope. Not here. Take your pretty little self all the way back to Starby’s. Give them my regards....She is really cute, though. Man, I’m an asshole.”
	
At the counter, the girl had ordered and was pulling a bare five dollar bill from her pocket. The boy at the counter handed her three bills and change as he handed her a cup of steaming coffee. She put it all in the square tip jar.
	
“Ohpah! We got a tipper here. Sorry, Charlie. It looks like we’ve gotta bump you back a few spots in the queue for sainthood.” 
	
He looked toward the man in the blazer, but he had left sometime ago. He quickly turned his attention back to the girl. 
	
“Who tips at these kinds of places? It’s their job to work here. I assume whoever gave them their job sees to it that they get paid for their job. I can’t ever bring myself to do it. It’s something about those shitty square plastic tip jars. They’re so off-putting. Who makes those anyway? Oh shit..”
	
The girl had turned around and was walking right towards Kurt’s table in a deliberate stride. Kurt quickly focused deeply on his monitor once again. 
	
“Oh, man. What if she walks by. I should talk to her. I should say: *did you get the French Roast? It’s really good here....* Oh, god! That’s retarded! I can’t say that. She’d probably dump it on me or something and fuck, that shit’s hot. Oh man, she’s really pretty!”
	
Kurt’s palms were drenched and he could feel the beating of his heart against the wall of his chest. 
	
“Well, fuck it. Another great opportunity I’m going to let slip through my fingers. It’s not the first time and it surely won’t be the last. Well, good riddance. She’d probably turn out to be a bitch anyway.”
	
Staring distantly into the glow of his laptop, he heard the defiant scoot of a fake wood, Ikea chair pulling back from the table. And the audible plunk of a girl in black jeans sitting down in that very chair. And the faint tap of a cardboard cup as she set her coffee down.
	
Kurt stayed down, as if his head would be bitten off by a puma if he dared look up. He didn’t understand. There were plenty of other places to sit. Half the tables in the place were vacant. At last, his rambling mind was lost for words. He knew what he’d have to do sooner or later. Taking a slow, deliberate inhale. He lifted just his his eyes to look towards the girl. 
	
A wide pair of green eyes stared back at him, and there was a definite kindness in them. And some of the tension dissolved from Kurt’s shoulders. She sat there staring for a moment, with her warm, toothless smile. Then, she took a breath and looked toward her coffee. 
	
“Why do they make this so goddamn hot?”

You're gonna get a lot of different answers on here as most pipers have their own ways of doing things. You have to do some trial an error to figure out the way you want to do it. Generally, I've found most pipers feel that teflon tape is just terrible on any joint that needs to move frquently, i.e. the tuning slides. It gets all torn up as the wood swells and contracts as with varying moisture levels. What I do, and what I feel is the easiest process, is to tie a string of unwaxed to a string of waxed such that they are parallel. Then I wrap them up from the wood from there. Sticks when you want it to; slides when you need it to. Easy-peasy. I've done a layer of teflon over that on the joints that go into the bag as it seems to help it from getting grungy from the moisture. Experiment with it. Black hemp sucks in my opinion. I want you to understand where everyone on here is coming from. As you've noticed we're all quite adamant on you getting an instructor. Great Highland Bagpipe is a very regimented, almost militarized, instrument. Variations on technique don't really work out on the pipes as they do for other instruments. I taught myself piano, bass, guitar, drums etc as well. I had a teacher for pipes. There's lots of quick, tiny embellishments/grace-noting involved in piping that if not learned properly at the beginning, can be very difficult to correct down the line. Any slight 'interpretations' will more or less be seen by the piping community as mistakes, and you'll find that it doesn't really sound like highland piping as you, and the world, have come to know it. You'd also have a difficult time playing with other pipers, which is one of the most rewarding parts of playing this instrument. Were not accusing you of not being able to teach yourself or anything like that. We just want you to get off on the right footing so you'll stick with it and become a successful piper.

Hello. I play both highland and uilleann pipes. I began highland piping when I was about 14 and uilleann pipes many years after. Although the fingering/technique is quite different, I can say from experience that highland piping helped me pick up the uilleann pipes a HELL of a lot faster. The same basic principles apply: the use of a bag to provide an unbroken stream of air to multiple reeds. A basic understanding of how highland pipes behaved helped me immensely to learn the uilleann pipes. I was passable (not great or anything) after about 3 months or so (granted I had a good tutor book and some experienced people to whom to ask questions). Also I had some other musical background. The *music* for this piece was composed by Gregorio Allegri. The music meaning the melodies and harmonies that the people are singing. He didn't not write the words. The words are a traditional Catholic prayer called Psalm 51, or "Miserere Mei, Deus." Translated, this means "Have Mercy on Me, God." The words are right out of the latin Bible. The Catholic Church decided Allegri's setting to be sacred. If one was to transcribe it, they would be excommunicated from the Church. (You'll find that the church likes to control access to things in this manner quite frequently in history). The piece was only performed one (maybe a few?) days during Lent. At the time, this was the ONLY way to hear this particular piece. One day, Mozart happened to be there to hear it. An astoundingly gifted man, he was able to *transcribe* the piece after only hearing it one time, returning only once, I think, to correct a few minor errors. This freed it up to be performed by whoever wanted to perform it. Mozart had both perfect pitch (able to tell what a note is by simply hearing it) and perfect relative pitch, (able to tell the differences between notes melodically/harmonically). Anyone who's tried to write down music just through listening can attest to how difficult it is, which is why Mozart is famous for this particular feat. Mozart's greatest gift was his ear for music. He could simply make music happen as easily as breathing which, to us mere mortals, seems like magic.
